key_insight: This paper shifts 3D asset generation from making objects look realistic to making them physically functional, with believable motion and articulation. It introduces a multi-agent pipeline that uses simulation feedback to improve geometry, appearance, and movement together.
problem_solved: Most 3D generation methods focus on visual fidelity and ignore whether an object can move, articulate, and interact plausibly in the real world. This paper addresses the gap between static-looking assets and physically grounded articulated assets.
method: Builds Artisan, an extension of Articraft that uses a multi-agent generation pipeline.
Incorporates physical simulation feedback to refine articulation and enforce physically plausible motion.
Targets richer asset properties beyond shape and texture, including collision-aware behavior and functional movement.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a path toward generating 3D assets that are useful not just for rendering, but also for robotics, simulation, gaming, and embodied AI. It also offers a benchmark-oriented framework for evaluating whether generated assets are actually usable in physical environments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing multiple agents generating and refining a 3D asset
Before/after comparison of visually realistic vs physically grounded articulated objects
Simulation feedback loop illustration with collisions and motion constraints
Benchmark dashboard with metrics for geometry, appearance, articulation, and physical plausibility
paper_title: Towards Physically Grounded Articulated 3D Assets: A Multi-Agent Pipeline and Benchmark
paper_authors: Xudong Cai, Ruijie Zhu, Haoliang Shang, Ruining Li, Marc Pollefeys
